target.title: fix: route bindings return the wrong agent when route identifiers contain separators
target.body:
Fixes an issue where route bindings can return the wrong agent when route cache key fields contain separator characters. The old cache key concatenated channel, account, peer, guild, team, and role fields with tab and comma delimiters. If any of those fields contained those same delimiters -- for example a peer named "room-1-guild-2" or role IDs containing commas -- two genuinely distinct routing contexts would share one cache key and the wrong cached route could be returned.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cache key is now a JSON-serialized array. Array elements are individually encoded by JSON.stringify, so no field value can accidentally form a delimiter when concatenated. The three remaining hyphen sentinel fallbacks (`guildId || "-"`, `teamId || "-"`) are replaced with `?? null` -- null serializes as a distinct JSON literal, so an absent field and the literal string "-" produce different cache keys.

## User Impact

Routing contexts whose peer, guild, team, or role identifiers contain tab, comma, or hyphen characters no longer risk receiving the wrong agent through a cache collision. The binding evaluation order, matching logic, and fallback behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Cache collision regression

Before fix (old `|| "-"` sentinels): an absent guildId and the literal string "-" produced the same cache key. The cached route for one returned the wrong agent for the other.

After fix (`?? null` in JSON array): absent fields serialize as `null`, distinct from any string literal including "-". Different routing contexts produce different cache keys and resolve independently.

New regression test (57/57 passed): `does not reuse a cached route when guildId is omitted versus the literal hyphen string` -- exercises the exact collision scenario the old sentinel permitted.

### Test coverage

- `resolve-route.test.ts`: 57 tests pass (3 new: peer+guild separator collision, role comma collision, and hyphen-sentinel collision). All three fail against the old delimiter-concatenated cache key.
- Scoped `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` pass.

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(gateway): reject non-object MCP app tool arguments
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users interacting with an MCP App widget could send non-object tool arguments through the Control UI bridge when a widget calls a tool. Arrays, `null`, strings, or numbers could be forwarded through `mcp.app.callTool` toward tool execution even though sibling MCP entry points already reject non-object `arguments`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI MCP App bridge now validates optional tool `arguments` at the server-method boundary before building the `tools/call` operation. Omitted arguments still normalize to `{}`, plain objects continue through unchanged, and arrays, `null`, strings, and numbers fail before `runtime.callTool()` is reached.

The change is intentionally limited to the Control UI `mcp.app.callTool` bridge. HTTP MCP, node-host invocation, standalone MCP App parsing, tool listing, message handling, and valid object-argument tool calls are unchanged.

## User Impact

MCP App widget tool calls now follow the same object-only argument contract as the other MCP tool-call entry points. Malformed widget-supplied arguments fail predictably before app tool execution, while valid widget calls continue to work as before.

## Evidence

AI-assisted: yes.

User-realistic call chain for the affected path:

```text
MCP App iframe/widget
  -> ui/src/components/mcp-app-view.ts:268-272 bridge.oncalltool forwards params.arguments
  -> src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.ts:106-115 handles mcp.app.callTool
  -> src/gateway/mcp-app-operations.ts:141-145 executes runtime.callTool(..., operation.params.arguments ?? {})
```

Before this fix, the Control UI handler cast `params.arguments ?? {}` to `Record<string, unknown>` without a runtime shape check. After this fix, the handler accepts omitted/plain-object arguments and rejects invalid values before constructing the tool-call operation.

Focused regression coverage added:

```text
src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.test.ts
  rejects non-object tool arguments before executing app tools

invalid arguments covered: [], null, "city=Paris", 42
expected result: "tool arguments must be an object"
execution guard: runtime.callTool is not called
```

Sibling surfaces checked:

```text
src/gateway/mcp-http.handlers.ts:100-105 already rejects non-object tools/call arguments.
src/node-host/invoke.ts:853-854 already rejects non-object arguments.
The standalone MCP App path is already parsed through the MCP operation schema before execution.
```
